missing.name: Lenth's method
missing.definition: Uses the many near-zero effects of an unreplicated design to estimate the noise, giving an objective cutoff for judging which effects are significant.
missing.quote: When the design is unreplicated, so there are no degrees of freedom for a standard error, we can still place an objective cutoff by using the idea of

missing.name: Pseudo standard error
missing.definition: A robust estimate of an effect's standard error: 1.5 times the median absolute effect, taken only over effects small enough to be plausibly noise.
missing.quote: (PSE) is a robust estimate of the standard error of an effect.

missing.name: Margin of error
missing.definition: Lenth's individual 95% cutoff, t(0.975, m/3) times the pseudo standard error; an effect whose magnitude exceeds it is significant on its own.
missing.quote: (ME) is the individual 95% cutoff: an effect whose magnitude exceeds the ME is significant on its own.

missing.name: Simultaneous margin of error
missing.definition: Lenth's stricter cutoff for testing all m effects at once, set so that all noise effects together stay below it with probability 0.95.
missing.quote: It is the stricter cutoff to use when scanning many effects at once.

missing.name: Half-normal plot
missing.definition: Absolute effects plotted against half-normal quantiles; noise effects fall on a straight line through the origin and real effects break away to the upper right.
missing.quote: Noise effects fall along a straight line through the origin; the real effects break away to the upper right.

missing.name: Allocating runs between two levels
missing.definition: For a fixed budget, split runs in proportion to sigma divided by the square root of cost; the even split is best only for equal variances and costs.
